I need to decide on an auction bid for Atlantic Avenue.

I'm evaluating whether to bid $276 for Atlantic Avenue. That would leave me with $662 cash, which clears the $600 New York rent. I'm also weighing the Orange rent potential with three houses.

Checking standard Monopoly rent tables for the Orange properties to verify exact payouts.

New York with three houses pays $600. The opponent currently holds three houses on all three Orange properties, so the worst-case hit is $550–$600. Winning at $276 leaves exactly $62 cash after clearing that rent. This sits right at my previous $280–300 cap. I'm now weighing the strategic value of holding Atlantic Avenue.

The Yellow group is split three ways. If I win, the yellows stay fully split. If p2 wins, they would own two yellows and could trade for a monopoly. p4 dropped out and wants to keep Ventnor so no one gets a cheap set. p2 has $1256 cash and is bidding aggressively for two yellows.

Mortgaging my three properties would give me roughly $305 in emergency cash. That could cover a second rent hit if needed. I am now weighing whether to bid $276 and drop out if p2 pushes higher.

p2 currently has no monopoly. If they acquire two yellows, they could trade with p4 for a full set. p4 already holds Ventnor and Park Place, so a yellow monopoly would be especially dangerous for me because p2 has $1256 to build.

Three houses on a yellow property pay $800–$850, which is worse than the Orange rent. Blocking p2 from two yellows is still worthwhile, but that only prevents one immediate pairing. p2 could still trade Marvin Gardens or reach an agreement with p4.

I have decided to bid $276. That keeps me within my $280–300 cap, and I will drop out if p2 pushes higher. Winning at that price gives me veto power over any yellow monopoly.

I am now weighing the trade-offs of winning at $276. That is slightly above the list price of $260, so I would be paying a small premium. My cash liquidity drops sharply from $938 to $662, which tightens my ability to cover future Orange rent hits.

If I win, I could later sell Atlantic to p2 or p4 for a profit, or keep it as a permanent block. Denying p2 development is the right long-term move since they are the cash leader and biggest threat.

I am also checking my position relative to the Orange properties from Baltic Avenue.

St. Charles and States are mortgaged, so they do not collect rent. The first live orange is St. James Place. I am calculating the distance from Baltic Avenue to St. James to assess how quickly I could reach it.

Baltic Avenue is space 2 and St. James Place is space 14, so the distance between them is 12 spaces. That means I would need to roll at least a 7 to land directly on an orange property, or simply pass through the zone.

The auction is on p1's turn, so I will not move until p3. That gives me at least one full turn cycle before my next roll. From Baltic Avenue, landing directly on St. James Place requires a roll of 12 or higher.

I will not raise above $276. I considered bidding $280 to signal commitment, but $276 is the minimum and preserves the most cash.
